utterances.text: My wife probably also heard it. So when I got back to the room, I told her to get up and get the children ready. Then I went over to my brother and my father to rouse them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What did you wear? What did you put on to wear?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I put on a pair of jeans and the top of a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take your weapon along?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I went to rouse my brother and my parents, I did not take my rifle with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So now you roused your parents and your brother. Then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: While I was doing this, my wife had roused the children. She was dressing them up when I came back, so I helped her with that, and to pack a few things for the children in a bag. We left the house and started up towards my brother and my father's house, and from there to Pudze's houses and in the direction of the shelter of Vrebac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you rouse anybody else on the way over there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we reached my uncle's house, I thought of Didaks. So I didn't know whether somebody had alerted them, so I ran to Manda's house. In fact, this is Branko Kupreskic's house, but this Manda Didak and her children -- Manda and Marica and her children lived there. So I told Marica that there was a possibility that we may be attacked and that they should get ready to go down to Niko Sakic's house. I told her to tell this to Manda, who was staying at another house. This was just a 20-metre detour, so I didn't spend more than a minute doing that. So with my wife, children, brother, his children, my parents and my brother's in-laws, we went down into that depression to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I had Ivica's weapon, that is, that hunting carbine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you got going, did you hear any shooting at that time or was it still silent?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was no shooting at the time. It was silent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: At the point when you were leaving home, was it still dark or had it already started to dawn?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Still dark. It was just before dawn, but it was still very dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Another question is why you carried weapons when you were actually fleeing.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, even before that, after the first conflict, after the 20th, on several occasions we had received information that it might be possible for an attack to take place from Borongaj. We would take all the weapons we had. We would take our families to places where there were more Croats, and then we would return -- we would leave them and we would return with our weapons. And if there would be an attack, then we would perhaps respond by shooting. So on that morning, I also took my rifle, thinking that it would be similar to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether you saw anyone en route, and just describe what you did as you went from your house to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we arrived at Niko Sakic's house, I saw a few of the locals. I saw Niko --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. When you say "locals", who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm talking about Croats who lived close to Niko Sakic's house. I'm talking about neighbours who lived near his house, and I remember Niko Sakic, Mirko, his son, Dragan Samija, Milutin Vidovic, Miroslav Pudze. There were also some women that were going to Niko Sakic's shelter. There was a basement where they took shelter. I remember that Milutin Vidovic, he was my best man, my kum, and he said, "Kum, you know, my wife stayed at home and there is a concrete roof there, so if anything happens, the concrete ceiling will protect them and it's near this Vrebac shelter. Since you have young children, you have a baby, perhaps it would be better for you to stay there with my family and you can have food prepared, et cetera," so that's exactly what I did. My mother and father were a bit in front of us. My brother was actually transporting his mother-in-law. We call this a wheelbarrow. He put her in the wheelbarrow, and I would help him every now and then, and the children were there. So they went to the Vrebac shelter, and I left my family at Milutin Vidovic's house, where I took them to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: At the point when you left your family at Milutin Vidovic's house, what was it like? Was it dawn, had it dawned already, or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't exactly daybreak, but you could see better.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You did not look at your watch? You cannot tell us the exact time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at that time I went to work early. I would usually wake up at quarter to 5.00, because that's when day would be breaking out. You could see that it was just beginning to dawn at quarter to 5.00. So since I know that period of time, I think it was around 5.00 at Niko Sakic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When you left your family at Milutin Vidovic's house, was there shooting at that moment already?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there wasn't any shooting yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Milutin Vidovic's house is closer, perhaps 30 or 40 metres away from the Vrebac shelter. I waited for my brother, and we together returned to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, as you were moving about, did you meet any soldiers, and when?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we were by the Pudja houses, we met -- I remember that this was by Ante Pudja's house. We met five or six soldiers on the road, on that road, and we also saw five or six -- well, it was dark, so I couldn't see more, but I saw from the back door of Ante Pudja's house -- it's not a proper road, but then there is a small road from Milan Samir -- or, rather, there's no road. There's a small meadow between Milan Samir's and Pudja's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So you took your family to Milutin Vidovic's house, and you encountered the military before you put your family up with them, or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When my brother and I proceeded from Niko Sakic's house, when Milutin told me to go there, when we left Niko Sakic's house and we started moving towards Zume, that's when I saw the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so your family was still with you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, my wife and my children, all the people I mentioned before were all there together. Only my mother and father were perhaps in front of us, some 50 metres, I don't know, in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you saw these soldiers, and could you describe them to us now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As I was passing by them, I saw that they wore black and camouflage uniforms, both kinds. They wore both one and the other. They had paint on their faces. It seemed to me that their faces were completely black, but I could see the shine in their eyes. They had rifles, and I could see that they had Osas, Zoljas, mortars or something -- I could not tell because it was still pretty dark, I could not -- RPGs. I didn't know exactly which weapons they had, but I had never felt that way before. I tried to get away as soon as possible. But I did not know what they wanted. I just saw them leaving this space between Milan Samir's and Ante Pudja's house, and they went up to the main road, and they moved toward Niko Sakic's house. They were taking that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were you terrified, perhaps, that this might be the Muslim army? Or precisely how did you identify whose army this was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they were coming from a part of the village that was predominantly Croat, where most of the population was Croat. And in addition to that, my mother and father were in front of us, and others were passing there, locals who were going to Niko Sakic's house, to the shelter. So I could not have assumed that these were Muslims, because how could Muslims come to Rotilj?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, it was your conclusion that these were Croat soldiers, is that right, judging on the road that they were coming from and all that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And there was no shooting then, at that time, when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: It was still dark?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was still dark, but I said that it was just before daybreak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When you met these soldiers, did you recognise any of them? Was there a single person that you knew, or that would have known you, that was amongst them? Somebody who would have said, "Hi, Zoran," for example?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, nobody said a word to me, and I did not recognise anyone. I looked at them only for a moment, and it was terrifying, and I looked away, and I thought, "Let's get out of here with the children. Let's get to Milutin Vidovic's house."

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice a special colour? That is to say, did any of them have belts that were of a special colour?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I noticed a few white belts, and also holsters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: White-coloured?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, white-coloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the weapons that this group of soldiers had?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were carrying weapons in their hands and down their arms. They were slung over their shoulders. I thought that they were automatic rifles. I said that I could not tell, because there was very little light coming from the sky, whether it was a mortar, Osa, Zolja, RPG, whatever. In my opinion, they were well armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask them, "Guys, where are you going?"

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never thought of doing anything of the kind. Perhaps that would make them take me with them. I can't even remember at that point whether I was carrying my baby or leading the other children or pushing the wheelbarrow. I just tried to get away as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, these soldiers, when you met them, you tried to get away as soon as possible; but in your mind, was there a process taking place as to where these soldiers were supposed to be going and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first thing that came into my mind -- and I was already on my way back; I was going to take my family to Milutin's house -- that we had already received information that there would be danger, and nothing came out of it, and it seemed to me that -- well, this was pretty serious this time. That's the only thing that crossed my mind. Then I thought perhaps, yes, there would be an attack, and these soldiers were going there to repel the attack, to fight. That's what had crossed my mind at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: That is your conclusion on the basis of the information that you had; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My brother and I returned to Niko Sakic's house, and at that moment, down from the depression, Manda and Marica Didak were coming out with their children, and Marica asked me -- or Manda, I can't remember which one -- where my wife was. I told her where she was and asked her whether she knew where the Vrebac shelter was, and she said that she didn't know, and I said, "Okay, I'll take you." My brother stayed on, and I went with the two of them and their children. I went back and I took them there, to the house. They wanted to be with my wife, so I took them to Milutin's house and left them there. Manda, that is, with two children, and Marica with two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then? Did you help the Didaks find accommodation? Did you send them somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I took them all the way to Milutin Vidovic's house, to the very threshold, but I did not enter the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So you came to that house, you left the Didaks there, and what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I started out to Niko Sakic's house, but when the shooting started, I was near Niko Vidovic's shelter, the shelter in the middle. It was there that I was, as far as I can remember, and then when the shooting started, I began to run. Perhaps it took me a minute or two to reach Niko Sakic's house. I would run for a while and then seek shelter, and then -- I would not run along the road, but there was a ditch. I don't know who was shooting, and from where. I could hear the shooting, so I sought shelter a bit, and then I ran to Niko Sakic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So when the shooting started, were you with someone, or were you on your own?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was on my own, but by Niko Sakic's house, where this shelter in the middle is, there were people in front of the shelter outside. There were women, actually, and a few civilians. When the shooting started, I know that they ran to the shelter by the house, and I went to Niko Sakic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you estimate how much time had passed from the moment when the soldiers passed by you to the moment when the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, my estimate would be, say, 20 minutes, perhaps half an hour, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: When the shooting began, what was the visibility like?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the shooting began, it had already dawned. It was daybreak. It was cloudy. As far as I can remember -- I can't remember. It seems to me that there was a bit of rain, a bit of a drizzle, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: At that time of the year, when does the day begin? When is dawn?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I think that dawn, daybreak, is around 5.00, because that's when I went to work. But it gets really light sometime before 6.00, say 5.30, 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What did you think was happening when you heard the shooting? At that point when the shooting began, afterwards, you started thinking about other things as you received information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I thought that this was an attack, and that the soldiers that I had met were repelling the attack, and that that was where the fighting was. But I did not know anything specific, nor did I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, could you have estimated where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard the shooting from the Kupreskic houses, my house, our houses. From that direction. I heard it coming from the road somewhere, down by the cemetery, too. As I was coming back from Zume to Niko Sakic's house, the shooting was coming from in front of me, a bit to the right-hand side and right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now try to show it on the large aerial photograph, and then later on you will mark it on a smaller copy of it. So will you now please take the pointer and approach the aerial photograph on the easel, please. Zoran, will you please first show the road you took when you were evacuating your family. Try to orient yourself on this map first. Find your house and then the way in which you evacuated your family.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is my house (indicating), and this is where I moved. I went to my parents' home --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in this -- what you did first. Start with the position where you all were together and being evacuated.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We went down to the depression, to Niko Sakic's house, and then down this road (indicating). I left my wife and family at Milutin Vidovic's house, and my brother took his to the Vrebac shelter, over here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you left your house and you went down towards the depression, was there a road there, or were there paths, or what did you follow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When you go from my uncle's house to the Sakics' house, it's just a path. This is what we used when we went down to visit people down there. It's just a simple path. It's not a road that a vehicle can use, just a footpath.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Is it a single footpath, or are there several of them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When you came to this forest, you could take -- it was just a meadow. It's a clearing. You could go on the edge of the forest. This footpath was on the edge of the forest. Before the open field, you had a forest, so to your left it would be all wooded. Or you could go through the woods, but only -- it was mostly used by the kids when they played. Yes, we could go -- this was also a footpath (indicating). There was a store there, so people from Zume used that path to go to the store and back. The asphalt road ended at Niko Sakic's house, here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Now show me, where did you encounter the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You cannot see it very well, but this is Niko Sakic's house (indicating), and this, Anto Pudja's and Milan Samir's houses (indicating). I saw some of them here, and some of them were actually on the road, perhaps five or six, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please take a seat now, and now please mark all these positions into the copy of the photograph you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph is D22/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: First, please mark the direction in which you moved. So let it be a line.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I again draw it first and then place it on the ELMO and show it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: If that is what is more convenient.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Will you please tell me again what to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: One full line to mark the way which you took from your homes to the place where you left your family, that is, Milutin Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That is the way you took, the direction you went to. Now mark with "X" the position where you encountered the military, and mark that position with "1." Once you are done, please place it again on the ELMO so that we can all see that, and then please point to that position.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the path we took (indicating). This is Milutin's house (indicating), and this is the Vrebac shelter (indicating), and this is the position where I encountered the military (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: And then please, finally, mark the spot where you were when you first heard the shooting.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Excuse me, how shall I mark it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: First put an "X" there, and then above it, put number "2."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I tender this photograph too. I'm not going to have the witness make any more markings on it. I think it completes this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were unable to see the point where number "2" is. I have objection (sic) to the exhibit being tendered, but I would like to see where the "2" is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: It is no problem to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, Zoran, please point on the ELMO where point "2" is. Did you mark number "2"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but it's marked in blue, and the ELMO does not show it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you also show us point "1" again, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here is number "1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: If we need -- if there are any further questions or clarifications, we're at your disposal. Then we can move on to the next segment of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So this document, D22/1, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran, now we're at the point where the shooting started and your position at the time when the shooting started. You thought that these soldiers came there to take on the fight as a defensive action, then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I came running to Niko Sakic's house, I saw Niko behind his house. In other words, when I arrived, he was on that side of the house. In passing, I asked him where the others were, and he said that they went running down into the depression, so I continued running in that direction myself. And I --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. There will be a lot of movement now, so perhaps you can help us by pointing to where you moved. Would you like to continue your narration, or would you like to keep on pointing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would prefer to just keep on narrating.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Go on, then.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: So in this depression, when I arrived, I saw Dragan Vidovic, Mirko Sakic, my brother Mirjan, Dragan Samir. Drago Grgic, I believe he was there also. They had all hidden, and if we look at this depression and that forest, between the Kupreskic and Sakics' houses, they were somewhere in the middle, perhaps closer to the Kupreskic -- they were around that path, and from the open field, the terrain starts sloping up, and that's where they were hiding. And as the shooting was going on, I joined them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in this position, or in some other position, could you notice anything burning?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After about 15, 20 minutes, perhaps even half an hour, we saw smoke, and I recall very well telling my brother, "Your and our father's house is on fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: How did you conclude that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The smoke was rising, and the forest is not very dense in that area, so my uncle's house could be seen, and behind it the smoke was rising. It looked to me that it was in the direction where that house was, so that's why I said it. And then to the right of it, also another plume of smoke started rising, and I thought, "There goes my house now." But I thought, "At least we're alive." So shortly thereafter, we moved further up. If you look from the depression up, off to the left, there's still a forest there, but it's narrower, so you could see better. We looked again to see whether these were indeed our houses that were on fire, and we couldn't see very well. A shell fell nearby. It looked to us as if it was very close, but it may not have been that close. So in front of us for another 20, 30 metres, the ground rose again, and then it sloped back downward, and that's where we felt that the shell had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to determine what exactly was on fire and was it really your houses that were on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not at that time. We didn't even make an attempt, except for that little lateral movement to try to ascertain what was burning. Later on, we learned that these were not our houses that were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Could you place in time when this was? Was it morning, late morning? Please try to place it as accurately in time as you can.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As this shooting had started somewhere around 5.30, 5.45, I don't know exactly when, about 15 minutes later or half an hour later, we started seeing this smoke. Then again, a short time thereafter, again it must be 10 or 15 minutes that that shell fell, and then we again ran back. It's only a distance of 30 to 40 metres, really. We heard the shooting in front of us. Then we hid there, and all this took place from the moment the shooting started, within an hour or two. All this happened in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So up until about 9.00, I mean, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Within a couple of hours. For a couple of hours, the shooting was the most intense early in the morning for an hour or two, and then it subsided, and then again up to three hours, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn of any deaths, any casualties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We heard of the first casualty, and that was Fahrudin Ahmic, a friend of ours, a friend of mine and Mico's.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: From whom did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When after this shooting, this couple of hours, when things quieted down a bit, we were concerned about our families. We did not know what had happened there. You could hear some explosions, some shells falling. Then we took an opportunity, Mico and I and Mirko Sakic, and decided to go over and see what had happened to our families. Near this middle shelter, Anto Vidovic, whose nickname was Satko, Mirko and I had passed, and Mirko had called out Mico, and then he went over there and then went back -- caught up with me and said -- he told me about Fahran.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Were you affected by the knowledge of that death?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Fahran is the young man we talked about when we talked about the whole group? 23 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you learn about further deaths? It would be useful if you could try to place it in time for me too.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we went over there, it could have been about 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning. I came to Milutin's house, and my brother went with Mirko to the Vrebac shelter. I was there at the door. I didn't get in. His wife came out, and from her I learned that there were additional dead bodies lying by the road. I asked about the children, and then I stayed there very briefly. Then went over to the shelter to check on my mother and father. I saw Zdravko Vrebac. Mico had already told him about Fahran. We were there briefly. I was there with my father, and we went back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic, shall we stop now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I had left it to you this time around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we'll adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 1.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of July, 1999, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
